WHERE account_id = 'acct_alice' AND currency = 'USD' AND balance_minor >= 10000; -- overdraft guard -- 1 row updated → proceed, else ROLLBACK with insufficient_balance INSERT INTO ledger_entries (txn_id, account_id, direction, amount_minor, currency, posted_at)
VALUES ('tx_01HWXB...', 'acct_alice', 'D', 10000, 'USD', now(6)); XA END 'tx_01HWXB...';
XA PREPARE 'tx_01HWXB...'; -- vote: YES

steps.title: PREPARE on shard_11 (credit Bob) — in parallel with shard_3 PREPARE
steps.action: In parallel with the debit, shard 11 prepares the credit. No overdraft guard on a credit; this almost always votes YES unless the account is frozen or the row is missing.
steps.codeOrCommand:
-- on shard_11 (Bob's home shard)
XA START 'tx_01HWXB...'; UPDATE account_balances
SET balance_minor = balance_minor + 10000, version = version + 1, updated_at = now(6)
WHERE account_id = 'acct_bob' AND currency = 'USD'; INSERT INTO ledger_entries (txn_id, account_id, direction, amount_minor, currency, posted_at)
VALUES ('tx_01HWXB...', 'acct_bob', 'C', 10000, 'USD', now(6)); XA END 'tx_01HWXB...';
XA PREPARE 'tx_01HWXB...'; -- vote: YES

steps.title: Both voted YES — coordinator writes COMMITTING and invalidates cache
steps.action: Coordinator updates its log to COMMITTING (the point of no return — from here we MUST drive commit on both shards, even through crashes). Before the commit lands, the balance cache entries for both accounts are invalidated so the next read hits the updated DB.
steps.codeOrCommand:
coordinator_log.update(txn_id, status="COMMITTING") # Cache invalidation BEFORE commit — window of stale is bounded by TTL on miss
redis.delete("bal:acct_alice:USD", "bal:acct_bob:USD") # Issue XA COMMIT to both shards
parallel { mysql_shard_3.xa_commit(txn_id) mysql_shard_11.xa_commit(txn_id)
}

steps.title: Redis DELs both cache keys
steps.action: Invalidation is synchronous before commit. The next balance read for either account is forced to go to the ledger and repopulate the cache with the post-transfer value.
steps.codeOrCommand:
DEL bal:acct_alice:USD bal:acct_bob:USD
# returns: 2 (both keys existed and were removed)

steps.title: XA COMMIT on both shards — locks released, balances become durable
steps.action: Both shards commit their prepared transactions. Locks drop. The balance changes and ledger entries are now durable. From the database's perspective the transfer is done.

steps.title: Coordinator finalizes log and publishes to Kafka
steps.action: Coordinator marks the txn COMMITTED in its log and produces a TransferCommitted event to Kafka — fire-and-forget from the user's perspective.
steps.codeOrCommand:
coordinator_log.update(txn_id, status="COMMITTED") # idempotency record (belt-and-suspenders)
ledger.execute("INSERT INTO txn_idempotency (idempotency_key, txn_id, response_body) VALUES (%s, %s, %s) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE txn_id=txn_id", ("8c3e9a1d-...", txn_id, response_json))

steps.title: Kafka appends TransferCommitted event
steps.action: Immutable audit record. Consumed independently by fraud, analytics, compliance reporting, and per-region replication.
steps.codeOrCommand:
kafka.produce( topic="wallet.transfer.committed", key="tx_01HWXB...", value={ "txn_id": "tx_01HWXB...", "from_account": "acct_alice", "to_account": "acct_bob", "amount_minor": 10000, "currency": "USD", "committed_at": "2026-04-24T14:08:33Z" }, acks="all"
)

steps.title: API returns 201 Created
steps.action: Coordinator signals success; API formats and returns the response.
steps.codeOrCommand:
return Response(status=201, body={ "txn_id": "tx_01HWXB...", "status": "committed", "amount_minor": 10000, "currency": "USD", "from_balance_minor_after": 15000, "to_balance_minor_after": 14200
})

steps.title: App shows success; balance re-fetched
steps.action: The app immediately re-requests /balance for Alice. The cache is cold (we invalidated it), so the read goes to the ledger and returns 15000 cents — the post-transfer value. End-to-end user-visible latency ~80–150ms depending on shard round-trip.

operations.title: Top-up from bank
operations.name: Top-up from bank
operations.description: User pulls $500 from their linked bank into the wallet. Wallet calls the Bank Connector, records pending, then settles on bank ack.

steps.title: User taps Add Money → $500
steps.action: App POSTs /top-ups with the linked bank account token and an idempotency key.

steps.title: API validates and claims idempotency
steps.action: Validates amount, currency, and that the bank_link_token belongs to the authenticated user. Inserts an idempotency record in MySQL to dedupe retries.
steps.codeOrCommand:
assert body.amount_minor > 0 and body.currency == "USD"
assert bank_links[jwt.sub].contains(body.bank_link_token) ledger.execute(""" INSERT INTO txn_idempotency (idempotency_key, txn_id, response_body, created_at) VALUES (%s, %s, NULL, now) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE idempotency_key = idempotency_key
""", ("2a9f4b8c-...", f"tp_{ulid.new}"))

steps.title: Auth validates token
steps.codeOrCommand:
claims = jwt_verify(token, pubkey)
assert not revocation_cache.contains(claims.jti)

steps.title: Coordinator records pending top-up
steps.action: Before calling the bank, we write a `pending` top-up row. If the bank call succeeds and we crash before recording success, recovery finds this row and reconciles from the bank's side.

steps.title: Bank Connector calls the partner bank
steps.action: External HTTPS call to the bank's pull-from-bank API. Uses our txn_id as the client_ref_id so any retry deduplicates on the bank's side.
steps.note: The money isn't in the wallet yet — banks take T+0 (FedNow/RTP) to T+1 (ACH) to settle. Wallet shows the amount as `pending` until the bank confirms settlement via webhook.

steps.title: Write pending top-up row (not yet available balance)
steps.action: The pending amount is visible as `pending_minor` on Alice's account but NOT in `available_minor`. User can see the top-up in the activity list but can't spend it yet.
steps.codeOrCommand:
BEGIN; INSERT INTO top_ups (id, account_id, amount_minor, currency, status, bank_txn_id, idempotency_key, created_at)
VALUES ('tp_01HWXC...', 'acct_alice', 50000, 'USD', 'pending', 'BNK-2026-04-24-9871234', '2a9f4b8c-...', now(6)); -- increment pending_minor only
UPDATE account_balances
SET pending_minor = pending_minor + 50000, version = version + 1
WHERE account_id = 'acct_alice' AND currency = 'USD'; COMMIT;

steps.title: TopUpSubmitted event (fire-and-forget)
steps.codeOrCommand:
kafka.produce( topic="wallet.topup.submitted", key="tp_01HWXC...", value={"txn_id":"tp_01HWXC...", "account":"acct_alice", "amount_minor":50000, "status":"submitted"}
)

steps.title: API returns 202 Accepted (pending settlement)
steps.action: The 202 status communicates that the request is accepted but terminal state is asynchronous. The client should poll or listen for the settlement event.
steps.codeOrCommand:
return Response(status=202, body={ "txn_id": "tp_01HWXC...", "status": "pending", "amount_minor": 50000, "currency": "USD", "estimated_settle_at": "2026-04-25T00:00Z"
})

steps.title: App shows $500 pending on Alice's account
steps.action: Some hours later (T+0 FedNow or T+1 ACH), the bank sends a settlement webhook → wallet updates available_minor and publishes wallet.topup.settled. Users see `pending` flip to `available` — that webhook-driven settlement is its own micro-flow.

operations.title: Balance read (cached)
operations.name: Balance read (cached)
operations.description: Ultra-hot path — every screen refresh hits this. 99% served from Redis.

steps.title: App requests balance on screen refresh
steps.codeOrCommand:
GET /v1/accounts/acct_alice/balance HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>

steps.title: API validates JWT ownership and delegates to Balance Service
steps.action: JWT must claim ownership of acct_alice. Fast local JWT verify + Balance Service call — no separate Auth hop for read-only paths (the Auth service's result is cached in-process for the JWT's lifetime).
steps.codeOrCommand:
assert jwt.claims.sub == owner_of("acct_alice")
return balance_service.get("acct_alice", "USD")

steps.title: Balance service reads from cache
steps.action: Cache-aside: try Redis first, fall through to ledger on miss.
steps.codeOrCommand:
key = f"bal:acct_alice:USD"
cached = redis.get(key)
if cached: return parse(cached) # hot path — 99% of reads

steps.title: Redis HIT — sub-ms response
steps.action: Key was populated on the last write or last miss-backfill. Returns immediately.
steps.codeOrCommand:
GET bal:acct_alice:USD
# O(1) in-memory dict lookup

steps.title: API formats and returns the balance
steps.action: Format minor units to major units only at the JSON edge — never in business logic. $150.00 display is computed as `15000 / 100`.
steps.codeOrCommand:
return Response(status=200, body={ "account_id": "acct_alice", "balance_minor": 15000, "pending_minor": 50000, "currency": "USD", "display": "$150.00", "pending_display":"$500.00"
})

steps.title: App renders balance
steps.action: End-to-end latency on cache hit: typically 15–30ms including network. Cache-miss path (~1% of reads) runs ~20ms slower due to the ledger read.

tradeoffs.chosen: Double-entry: every transfer is two rows (debit + credit) in ledger_entries
tradeoffs.rationale: Balance-only makes bug-induced drift invisible — if the credit side silently drops, nobody notices until someone sums the system. Double-entry makes the invariant SUM(ledger_entries) = 0 across the system, which the nightly audit job checks. Cost is 2x the rows, but ledgers are cheap compared to the cost of losing trust.

tradeoffs.chosen: Materialized wallet_balances row updated inside the same transaction as the ledger
tradeoffs.rationale: SUM-on-read is O(ledger_rows) per balance check — fine at 100 users, catastrophic at 100M. Materialized balance is O(1) but can drift if a bug writes the ledger without updating the balance. We prevent drift by keeping both writes in one transaction and auditing nightly.

tradeoffs.chosen: SERIALIZABLE for the critical transfer path, optimistic retry at the service layer on conflict
tradeoffs.rationale: SERIALIZABLE prevents write skew (e.g., two concurrent transfers both passing the balance check before either writes) that READ COMMITTED allows. The cost is retries under contention; the service layer catches serialization failures and retries up to 3 times before returning 409 — which caps tail latency.

tradeoffs.decision: Strong consistency vs eventual consistency across shards
tradeoffs.chosen: Strong consistency within a shard, 2PC or saga across shards
tradeoffs.rationale: Most transfers are within-shard (both users hash to the same shard) and use a single local SERIALIZABLE transaction. Cross-shard transfers use a saga: reserve funds on the source shard, commit on the destination, release or compensate. This avoids 2PC's coordinator-failure pitfalls at the cost of a visible pending state for a few seconds.

tradeoffs.decision: Instant top-up UX vs rail finality
tradeoffs.chosen: Two-phase: expose a pending balance immediately, flip to available after rail settlement
tradeoffs.rationale: ACH can take 1-3 days to settle; users won't wait. Two-phase balance (available + pending) lets us show the money while gating actual spend until settlement. The risk is a failed settlement requiring a reversal — we mitigate with per-user top-up velocity limits and a fraud model that blocks high-risk new accounts from spending pending funds.
